_format: Runewright seed file — read by scripts/gen_vectors.dart to produce corpus.json. All cell indices are in canonical q×r flat order (see docs/GRID_ORDERING_v2.md). active_cells values must be inscribable (hex distance ≤ 8 from center, i.e. max(|q|,|r|,|q+r|) ≤ 8); valid indices range from 62 to 406 but are NOT contiguous. Center (0,0) = index 234. Element indices: 0=neutral, 1=fire, 2=air, 3=water, 4=earth. border_activations order: [fire=0, air=1, water=2, earth=3].

vectors.description: all-zero grid: stays empty forever, no outputs (smoke test for stepper wiring)

lone center cell at index 234 (q=0,r=0): under ink rules (RULESET_VERSION 2) a cell with 0 active neighbours is not a tip (Rule B requires exactly 1) and not axis-complete (Rule A requires a full antipodal pair). It stays alive forever under Rule D (no-deaths) but never spawns neighbours. All outputs are zero through any T.

UPDATED RULESET_VERSION 2 (ink). Full ring-8 (the maximal inscribable ring, 48 cells; same active_cells as neg_mask_abuse). Under ink rules, each ring-8 cell has exactly 2 active neighbours (adjacent ring cells) so no Rule B fires from the ring itself; border activations arise from the interior filling via Rule A/B spreading outward through the buffer zone and touching ring-12 by T=8. Border [7,5,7,5] is stepper-verified under RULESET_VERSION 2 (was [7,8,7,8] under v1 Conway neutral). The T=3 companion (mask_boundary_zero) remains [0,0,0,0] because the first contact still occurs after T=3.

Circuit-side discharge of the masking property behind neg_mask_abuse: same active_cells as first_border_activation/neg_mask_abuse (full ring-8), but T=3 instead of T=8/T=4. The stepper confirms generation 3 is where activity actually starts (see neg_mask_abuse), so this proves the circuit's own masked output is genuinely [0,0,0,0] at T=3 - not just that an attacker's declared non-zero value gets rejected (that half is a SNARK public-input-binding property, deferred to the M3.4 end-to-end tamper smoke test), but that the circuit computes the correctly-masked zero in the first place.

RULESET_VERSION 2 (ink). Closes the CIRCUIT_IO.md §11.8 seam (forged death / monotonicity): a 2-cell tip at (7,0)/(8,0) -- flat indices 388/406, the latter being the documented max inscribable index -- grows via Rule B exactly one cell per generation toward the border at (12,0): (9,0) born gen1, (10,0) gen2, (11,0) gen3, border touch at gen4. Each step's birth condition (Rule B requires the tip to have EXACTLY ONE active neighbor) is causally dependent on the immediately-preceding tip cell still being active (Rule D / no-deaths) -- if a monotonicity bug let any intermediate tip die, the chain stops growing right there and the border touch never happens (or happens at the wrong generation), changing border_activations, dominance_trajectory, AND supreme_dominance_flags all at once. This is the property the abstract §11.8 vector (a witness can't express a forged death at all -- next_grid is derived, not witnessed, see CIRCUIT_IO.md §10.5/§10.10) is actually subsumed BY: this seed is the concrete positive vector that makes that subsumption real rather than asserted. Stepper-verified directly (scripts/gen_vectors.dart not yet run against this seed): border_activations/dominance_trajectory/supreme_dominance_flags are all-zero through T=1..3 and only become non-zero at T=4 -- confirming the touch is genuinely contingent on three full generations of unbroken persistence, not an artifact of the seed's shape. Gen4 also happens to be a pulse generation (cadence=4): the serif-flare condition on (12,0) shares the exact same upstream dependency on (11,0) staying alive, so the coincidence reinforces this vector's coverage rather than confounding it -- two ink rules, one shared dependency, either of which a monotonicity bug would equally break.

RULESET_VERSION 2 (ink). Pins the (g+1)%4 pulse cadence at g=3 (stepCount=4). Seed: two-cell tip anchor=(0,-7)=227 and tip=(0,-8)=226 on the negative-r axis. The tip at d=8 extends outward one cell per gen via Rule B: d9 at gen1, d10 at gen2, d11 at gen3. At gen3 (InkStep.step called with generation=4, 4%4==0: PULSE), Rule B extends to (0,-12) fire border and serif (Rule E) fires for two additional border cells with exactly one active neighbour -- (-1,-11) in the fire zone and (1,-12) in the air zone -- producing a total of 3 border contacts instead of 1 (the Rule-B-only contact at gen4 without the pulse). This causes air/wind to become supreme at gen3 (fire=2, air=1 activations; after decay d=2 fire drops to 0 leaving air=1 dominant) which would NOT happen at gen4 without the pulse. Any wrong cadence (off-by-one in (g+1)%4) shifts the contact generation and changes traj/sup, breaking the vector. T=5 includes gen3 (pulse) and gen4 (one further Rule B step, no extra border contact since the serif at gen3 seals no tip neighbours in the fire chain).

RULESET_VERSION 2 (ink). Exercises Rule A gap-fill + multi-gen Rule B + serif (Rule E) together. Seed: two cells with a single-cell gap -- (0,-6)=228 and (0,-8)=226 -- separated by the dead cell (0,-7) which has both as antipodal neighbours on the dir2/dir5 axis. Rule A fires at gen1, creating (0,-7) (the gap-fill birth). Neither seed cell has any active neighbour at T=0 (they are 2 apart, not adjacent), so NO Rule B fires in gen0 -- the chain only starts after the gap-fill. After gen1, the chain {(0,-6),(0,-7),(0,-8)} has tips at both ends; the outward tip at (0,-8) extends to (0,-9) at gen2, (0,-10) at gen3, ..., (0,-11) at gen6, reaching (0,-12) fire border at gen7 (stepCount=8, 8%4==0: PULSE). The pulse at gen7 triggers serif for (-1,-11) fire and (1,-12) air in addition to the Rule B extension, creating fire=2 + air=1 activations identical to pulse_boundary but one pulse period later. Air supreme at gen7 (traj[7]=2). A circuit that omits Rule A produces no chain (both cells isolated, 0 active neighbours → no Rule B, no growth) and outputs all-zero border/traj/sup -- unambiguous mismatch. A circuit with wrong Rule B length (single-pass instead of two-pass) miscomputes tip extension and misses the border contact at gen7.

RULESET_VERSION 2 (ink). Three parallel fire-zone chains produce enough fire pressure to reach supreme dominance, then the fire elemental CA runs for the remaining T, exercising the reindexed (rule-1)*14 lookup in FLAT_TRANSITION. Chains: F1 anchor=(0,-7)=227 tip=(0,-8)=226 toward fire (0,-12); F2 anchor=(-3,-4)=158 tip=(-4,-4)=136 toward fire (-8,-4); F3 anchor=(-5,-2)=117 tip=(-6,-2)=97 toward fire (-10,-2). All three reach their border cells at gen3 (pulse, stepCount=4). Each chain's serif at gen3 produces 2 fire + some air/cross activations; with three chains the fire total far exceeds air: fire=21, air=5 by T=7. Fire achieves supreme dominance at gen3 (dominant=fire=1, traj[3..6]=1, sup[3..6]=1). Gens 4-6 evolve under fire rules, exercising FLAT_TRANSITION[0..13] = (1-1)*14 + state*7 + nb. A circuit with wrong reindexing (circuitIdx*14 instead of (circuitIdx-1)*14 for fire) indexes into the neutral row offset, producing different survival/birth outcomes and a divergent trajectory.

RULESET_VERSION 2 (ink). Three chains pointing toward three different border zones (fire, air, water) accumulate pressure roughly simultaneously, holding a multi-zone tie across multiple generations so that ceil(D/k) in _decayAtMaxPressure is exercised with k≥2 more than once. Chains: fire F1=(0,-7)=227/(0,-8)=226 toward (0,-12); air A1=(7,-6)=382/(8,-6)=400 toward (12,-6); water W1=(0,7)=241/(0,8)=242 toward (0,12). All tips are at d=8, pointing away from center. At gen3 (pulse): all three chains simultaneously reach their respective border zones via Rule B + serif, producing fire≈2, air≈3, water≈2, earth=1 (water serif clips (-1,12) earth zone). After decay (max=air, k=1, dec=ceil(2/1)=2): air drops, fire/water tied → dominant=0. Through T=6 the pressures remain roughly balanced; no element achieves sole dominance across all 6 gens. All-zero dominance_trajectory + non-zero border_activations [4,3,4,1] with non-zero pressures confirms the tie was sustained (never resolved to a lone leader). Exercises ceil(D/k) with k≥2 on subsequent gens (e.g. gen4: fire/water tied, k=2, dec=ceil(3/2)=2 vs wrong ceil(3/1)=3 would over-decay one zone and break the balance).

vectors.description: RECLASSIFIED 2026-06-16: this is a SNARK public-input-binding check, not a Runewright circuit-constraint vector - commitment is a return value, not an input, so nargo execute structurally cannot accept a 'declared' value that disagrees with what the circuit computes (§10.4 is enforced by construction: there is no path to a different value). The circuit-relevant half (commitment is always the real Poseidon2(packed_grid), never something else) is discharged by every positive vector's frozen, Noir-sourced commitment (anchor_empty, anchor_single_center, first_border_activation, mask_boundary_zero). The remaining half - that bb verify rejects a proof whose public-input bytes were tampered with post-hoc - is a property of UltraHonk's public-input encoding, not of this circuit; deferred to a single end-to-end tamper smoke test in M3.4 (prove, flip one byte of the commitment in the public inputs, confirm bb verify rejects). Valid grid (lone center cell) kept here as the input fixture for that future smoke test.
